patterns.name: The moats left when anyone can build
patterns.why_it_travels: A checklist people screenshot and argue over. Strongest when you name your own moat with a number.
examples: NickADobos: if software is dead, how do you monetize (~57k)

patterns.name: Help IRL businesses/people move to AI
patterns.why_it_travels: Moves the debate from dev Twitter to the real world; money and helpfulness in one line.
examples: levelsio: get rich helping IRL businesses (~186k)
gregisenberg: every app built around humans clicking gets rethought (~47k)

patterns.name: Do not blame the agent, blame the system
patterns.why_it_travels: Two-line reframe with a clear villain. Easy to transplant into any domain (manuals, schools, forms).
examples: mattpocockuk: blame the codebase for the bad test (~99k)
mattpocockuk: GLOSSARY.md makes the agent speak my language (~45k)

patterns.name: "Software is dead" round two: backlash and jokes
signals: directionally correct but a bit early
patterns.why_it_travels: Yesterday's mega thesis now gets replies, counters and one-line jokes; anyone can join with a take.
examples: shl: Software is dead / Work for the government (~182k)
levelsio: Grok says directionally correct but early (~70k)
jackfriks: just keep making useful things (~32k)

patterns.name: Not doom: an explosion of personal creativity
signals: anyone can make their own personal software
patterns.why_it_travels: Optimistic reframe of a scary claim. Best paired with a real non-coder receipt.

patterns.name: New frontier model drop → instant bake-offs
signals: back to codex and claude code
patterns.why_it_travels: Launch day plus side-by-side verdicts; people want a fast answer to "is it good?".
examples: dhh: shipped Omarchy PRs with Wonder (~50k)

patterns.name: For normies, the magic is design
patterns.why_it_travels: Shifts focus from benchmarks to experience, which matches visual education.
examples: clairevo: Muse is the best personal agent for normies (~19k)

patterns.name: Self-improving agent swarms
patterns.why_it_travels: Big promises plus simple step lists; high reach but often promo. Skip unless you have a real receipt.

patterns.name: AI is now cheap, small and everywhere
signals: same month AI models became capable
swan song for the Big Studio Era
patterns.why_it_travels: A concrete then-vs-now contrast; supports "free education for everyone".

patterns.name: AI-assisted nostalgia keeps compounding
patterns.why_it_travels: Playable zero-install demos people Turing-test and share.

patterns.name: One-word teaser posts
patterns.why_it_travels: Pure brand reach before a launch. Not transferable to a 14-follower account.

patterns.name: Off-topic reach bait
patterns.why_it_travels: Big reach, no AI receipt. Skip for @bobbyships.
examples: levelsio: everyone makes this mistake once (~446k)
clairevo: white is my color, 3 boys (~9k)

Power users are building entire swarms of AI agents that learn, adapt, and improve themselves.”

virals_narrative: Outside the watchlist, Mon–Tue is a Meta news cycle plus round two of "software is dead". Meta's Muse Wonder launch (~191K) triggered instant bake-offs: Theo's Opus 5.5 vs GPT-6.1 Sol vs Muse Wonder bug-fix race (~215K) and "atrocious at UI" (~47K), Riley Brown's "5 hours, back to Codex and Claude Code" (~65K), and DHH shipping Omarchy PRs with Wonder (~50K). Agent swarms are the reach magnet: Bindu Reddy's self-improving revenue agents (~2.19M), Anthropic's distillation-attack defense post (~1.02M), and a reverse-engineer-any-app agent pitch from 0xCodila (~689K, reads like token promo). The "software is dead" debate turns into jokes and counters: Sahil Lavingia's "Work for the government" (~182K), Riley Brown's "I've been downloading apps like crazy" (~140K), Nick Dobos asking how anyone monetizes (~57K), and Greg Isenberg saying every app built around humans doing the clicking gets rethought (~47K). Nikita Bier's "$2B game drops the same month AI can make comparable experiences" (~363K) and Ethan Mollick's "19 phone-sized models beat GPT-4" (~29K) carry the "cheap and everywhere" story. For @bobbyships the sharpest angles are moats → your audience is the moat, Matt's "blame the codebase, not the agent" → blame the 84-page manual, not grandma, and Claire Vo's "the magic is design" → visual education beats walls of text.
